title: Quantification of Gel Bands by an Image J Macro, Band/Peak Quantification Tool
author: Kenji Ohgane
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7vghn3w
materials: Quantification of an western blot image

steps.title: Install ImageJ Macro
steps.instruction: Download the _BandPeakQuantification.ijm macro file and place it in a directory under the ImageJ plugins directory (e.g., Applications > ImageJ > plugins).

substeps.instruction: Restart ImageJ to automatically recognize the macro via the '_' prefix, or navigate to Help > Update Menu to refresh the menu.
Note: Subdirectories can be used within the plugin directory to organize multiple macros.

steps.title: Prepare Image
steps.instruction: Open the target image (e.g., File > Open Samples > Dot blot).

substeps.instruction: If necessary, invert the image via Edit > Invert so that background is low intensity (black) and signals are high intensity (white).
Adjust contrast via Image > Adjust > Brightness/Contrast or Process > Enhance Contrast to facilitate ROI selection, but do not click 'Apply' or check 'normalize' as this alters the image data.

steps.title: Define Regions of Interest (ROIs)
steps.instruction: Identify and register the bands/dots to be quantified using the ROI Manager.

substeps.instruction: Open the ROI Manager via Analyze > Tools > ROI Manager and enable 'Show all' and 'Labels'.
Place a rectangle or circle on a band and register it by pressing Cmd+t (Mac), Ctrl+t (Windows), or clicking 'Add' in the ROI Manager window.
Repeat for all bands to be quantified. Note: ROIs do not need to be the same size; define appropriate sizes for each band based on intensity (higher intensity generally requires larger ROI).

steps.title: Run BandPeakQuantification Macro
steps.instruction: Execute the macro from Plugins > BandPeakQuantification and configure the quantification parameters.

substeps.instruction: Set 'Background with (pixels)' to determine how much to expand the ROI for background estimation.
Select 'Estimate background from' option: 'all' (expands ROI in all directions), 'top/bottom' (applicable for rectangles), or 'sides'.
Select the background estimation method: 'median' (default, more robust against outliers) or 'mean'.
Keep 'reset scale' checked if the image scale (µm/pixel) is set; note that the scale will be reset upon running.

steps.title: Export Macro Results
steps.instruction: Review the quantification results in the Results window.

substeps.instruction: Identify 'signal' as the background-corrected integrated intensity and 'total' as the integrated intensity without correction.
Save the results as a CSV file by right-clicking the results window, or copy and paste the data into Excel.

steps.title: Alternative: Traditional Lane-Profile Method
steps.instruction: Perform quantification using the standard ImageJ gel analysis tools as a comparison.

substeps.instruction: Create a horizontal rectangle ROI for the first lane and press Cmd+1 (Mac), Ctrl+1 (Windows), or Analyze > Gels > Select First Lane.
Select subsequent lanes and press Cmd+2 (Mac), Ctrl+2 (Windows), or Analyze > Gels > Select Next Lane; repeat for all lanes.
Press Cmd+3 (Mac), Ctrl+3 (Windows), or Analyze > Gels > Plot Lanes to generate lane profiles.
Draw baseline lines at the bottom of the peaks to account for uneven background.
Use the Wand tool from the toolbar to click the peaks (ensuring the peak area is closed by lines) to calculate the peak area in the Results window.
